what: Both paper entries of the first 14 hours were not touches. MADE: the word 'MADE' in a Trump endorsement of an Oklahoma candidate matched a coin that happened to have 50 buys that hour. BAG: someone sent 1.75 % of supply to the ANSEM fee wallet unasked; stopped at -0.325 SOL.
why: The contract assumed a touch is something a person does. The resolver measures string equality and the wallet feed measures arrivals, and anyone can cause either. The breadth screen cannot repair this: it checks the coin, not the intent.
rule: Next contract: a touch needs evidence of intent (a $ticker or mint in the person's own words, or a buy the person signed). Capitalised words in a sentence and transfers into a public wallet are logged, never traded.

what: RI-01 was superseded by RI-02 after 1 closed trade, and its open forecasts were voided unanswered.
why: RI-01's stop lost 0.325 SOL every time it fired, above the contract's own S1 bar of mean loss < 0.3 SOL, and nothing but the 24 h clock removed a trade that was going nowhere (BAG sat 4 h 15 min). The operator's doctrine is to lose small and fast; the contract did not encode it. The forecasts assumed the leg would run to 40 closes or a KILL and gave no odds to an early rule change by the operator.
rule: Before freezing a contract, work each exit's booked loss against each gate by arithmetic, and forecast the operator superseding the leg early as its own question.

what: RI-02 was frozen without the intent rule the first lesson left for the next contract, and was superseded by RI-03 within minutes, before any entry.
why: Claude changed only what was asked (the stop) and did not start the new contract from the journal's section 6, as the process requires. It then handed the gap to the operator as an open question instead of ruling it. Ruled through RI in decisions/2026-10-03-ri02-holes.md.
rule: A new contract id starts from every rule in section 6. Open choices are ruled through ops/decide.py and journalled, not handed to the operator.

what: The paper book marks every fill at the deepest pair's quote, as if 1 SOL moved nothing. Standing estimate of what a real round trip loses to price impact: 4 x size / pool liquidity, which with SOL at $119 is 2.4% of the trade at the $20,000 liquidity floor, on top of the 2.5 % fees. BAG (entry liquidity $63,523) reads -0.333 SOL after the haircut against -0.325 on paper.
why: The contract models fees and nothing else, so every paper figure is the figure of a fill that cannot be had. The estimate assumes a constant-product pool whose quoted liquidity is both sides, uses the entry snapshot only, and has no real fill behind it: a stop sold into a falling pool will do worse than this.
rule: Next contract: book every paper trade net of the fill haircut (4 x size in USD / entry liquidity) as well as fees, judge the gates on the haircut figures, and set the liquidity floor from the trade size so the haircut at the floor stays under 1 %.

what: RI-03's intent rule reads a $ticker inside a retweet or a report as the person's own words. 3 of the 4 intent touches so far were retweets (PUSA; USELESS and PENGU from one HolderScan post) and the fourth was StonkFun reporting its own revenue. None passed the screen, so nothing was entered on one.
why: The rule asks whether the post carried the ticker, not who wrote the sentence. A retweet is the person passing on someone else's post, and a report is an account describing its own token. The operator ruled 2026-10-03 that RI-03 stands as frozen; the share and the 24 h result of retweets against own words are now forecast instead (mk_rtshare, mk_rtgap).
rule: Next contract: a retweet, or a report of an account's own token, is not intent. Only a $ticker or mint the person typed in an original post or a quote, or a buy their wallet signed, may enter.

what: The RI-03 entry forecasts (70d5891ac0bd first entry by 10-17 at 45 %, 5bbb27dbcd25 three closes by 10-31 at 30 %, 51134d6f82cd an X entry by 10-31 at 40 %, 3cd6a1d57f1b forty closes at 5 %) were made on one intent touch in 36 hours. The journal counts four: Claude's hand count looked only for mints and phrases that began with $, and missed tickers.
why: The count behind the forecasts was a one-off script, not the instrument. The forecasts stay as written (operator ruling 2026-10-03). A later miss on them is to be read against this undercount first, not as the model being wrong about how often people touch coins.
rule: Count from the journal's own metric (`python ops/journal.py market`) before writing a rate forecast, never from a one-off script.

what: The sensor saw 268 touches on 2026-10-04 against a range of 60-170; 2026-10-03 had closed at 185, already above the top of the range.
why: The range was scaled from 79 touches in the first 13.7 h of one day and then cut further for a Sunday. The weekend discount was a guess with no data behind it, and the full 2026-10-03 (185) showed the part-day pace understated the whole day; the roster posted more on Sunday, not less.

what: 56 touches named a coin on 2026-10-04 against a range of 10-45; the naming share held at 21% (56 of 268), close to the quarter assumed.
why: The share was right; the miss came entirely from the touch count it was multiplied by, which was set too low (see 86293fe703b3). The range should have been built on the full previous day, not a part-day.

what: 12 screened touches showed intent on 2026-10-04 against a range of 1-6; 3 of the 12 were retweets (rtshare 0.25).
why: The range rested on 3 and 1 intent touches over two part-days, too few to say how lumpy the count is. With touches up to 268 and naming at 21%, intent at 12 is about 4% of touches, near the 2026-10-02 rate (3 of 35), so the count scales with volume and the range should have scaled with it.

what: RI-03 made two paper entries on 2026-10-05, 12 days early: EWZ at 15:53Z and CBRS at 20:43Z. Both were stonk.fun retweets of Sunrise/Backpack posts announcing tokenised stocks (iShares MSCI Brazil ETF, Cerebras) on Solana. Both passed the screen easily: liquidity $605k and $1.29M, ages 16 and 38 min, EWZ 102 buys and 0 sells in its first hour. EWZ took half at +101 % 20 minutes after entry.
why: The 45 % rested on one intent touch in 36 h, a hand count that missed tickers (the journal later counted four), and on the picture of a person naming a memecoin. What actually entered was a launch platform passing on listing announcements for tokenised stocks. Those have the deep liquidity and buy counts the screen asks for, and RI-03 reads the retweeted $ticker as intent. The market half held (intent averaging 4.07 a day against the 1 a day forecast in ae203cc53688); the screen let these through.
rule: Next contract: listing announcements by platform or protocol accounts (stonk.fun, Raydium, Sunrise, Backpack) are not touches, and tokenised stocks (Backpack Securities issues) are kept out of the screen.

what: The X feed made both RI-03 entries on 2026-10-05 (EWZ, CBRS), 26 days before the deadline. Both came from stonk.fun retweeting tokenised-stock listings; Truth Social made none.
why: The 40 % came from the same undercount of intent touches (one in 36 h by hand; the journal counted four) and was set low for that reason. The belief that X is where tickers get posted was right. What it missed is that the tickers X carries in volume come from platform accounts announcing listings, not from people. Intent averaged 4.07 a day against the 1 a day in ae203cc53688, so the market held and the screen passed what it was shown.

what: 43 screened touches showed intent on 2026-10-05 against a range of 1-6. About 33 of them came from one Raydium post listing its September listings ($DOGE $NKE $SPHR $HTZ ...). The other ten posts were stonk.fun and Raydium announcing the EWZ and CBRS tokenised-stock listings and stonk.fun's revenue report.
why: The range treated intent touches as independent Poisson arrivals at about 2.8 a day. The metric counts one row per ticker screened, so a single list post from a platform account adds dozens at once, and the count clumps. Even leaving the list post out, the day ran about 10, above the top of the range. The 10-04 lesson had already said the count scales with volume and the range had not been widened enough.

what: RI-03 closed its third paper trade on 2026-10-06, 25 days before the 2026-10-31 deadline: EWZ (+1.209 SOL, take-half then time), RACE (-0.033, stale after 15 min) and CBRS (+0.131, time). Forecast said 30 %.
why: The 30 % rested on about 5 intent touches a week reaching the screen. The journal's own count ran 12, 43, 16 and 13 a day over 10-04..10-07 (the 10-04..10-31 market forecast 3cee1eb3bd34 stands at 3.04 a day against its 1-a-day bar), so the rate fed into the forecast was several times too low. The screen's 1-in-10 pass held roughly (5-7 % passed); the miss is the hand-counted market rate already flagged in lesson 03e32b4bb68e, plus platform accounts posting tickers in volume.

what: 16 screened touches showed intent on 2026-10-06 against a range of 1-14; 6 of the 16 were retweets (rtshare 0.375), out of 176 touches, so intent ran 9 % of touches.
why: The range assumed intent runs 1-4 % of touches and scaled that to 80-320 touches. The days since run 12/268 (4 %), 43/148, 16/176 (9 %) and 13/131 (10 %): the share is higher than assumed and clumps when a platform account posts several tickers at once. An 80 % range on this count needs a top near 25, not 14.

what: The forecast was voided: the resolver gave up after 12 tries with the 24 h window still open. The market table now reads the median 24 h return of the 51 coins screened on 2026-10-05 as +0.0 %, which would have landed inside the -15 %..+5 % range.
why: The resolver's retry budget ran out before the last screened coin's 24 h window closed, so a forecast that was answerable was scored as never defined. The medians of 0.0 on 10-03, 10-05 and 10-06 also suggest many screened coins never trade again after the touch, so the median measures dead coins as much as drift.

what: The forecast was voided a second time the same way: the resolver gave up after 12 tries with the 24 h window of the last coin screened on 2026-10-07 still open. The market table now reads the median 24 h return of the 24 coins screened that day as -0.7 % (share up 17 %), inside the -20 %..+10 % range.
why: The same measurement gap as 30e791aea8bd for 10-05: the forecast's deadline is the day after the screening day, but a coin screened late in the day has its window open until that same hour the next day, and 12 tries run out before then. The belief about the market (a median near zero, dominated by coins that never trade again) was right both times; the instrument scored an answerable question as undefined.
rule: Next contract: a ret24 forecast resolves only after the last screened coin's 24 h window has closed; the resolver waits for the window, it does not spend its retry budget against it.

what: 36 touches on 2026-10-09 against a range of 115-270, all logged between 00:00Z and 10:32Z. The X stream went quiet after 10:32Z, the heartbeat stopped at 11:58Z (06:58 Central) when the machine went down, and state/feeds.json, state/positions.json and monitor/heartbeat.json came back as zero-filled files of their old sizes. From 18:42Z the guard restarted the sensor every 5 minutes and it died at startup on the zero-filled feeds.json (JSONDecodeError), so nothing was logged for 24 h and 2026-10-10 stood at 0 touches at 11Z. The 2026-10-10 run backed the zeroed files up and reset them to their empty defaults.
why: The forecast assumed the instrument runs. A market forecast is scored on what the sensor logged, so a day the sensor was down scored as a market miss; the range itself (full days ran 131-336) was fine. The sensor treats a state file that exists but does not parse as fatal while a missing one is fine, and the guard restarts into the same crash forever because it checks the heartbeat, not the crash.
rule: Next contract: a market forecast for a UTC day on which the sensor logged fewer than 20 of 24 hours is voided, not scored. A state file that does not parse is renamed aside and treated as missing, so the sensor starts instead of dying on it, and the guard alerts when the sensor dies at startup twice running.

what: 0 screened touches showed intent on 2026-10-09 against a range of 3-28. Only 4 touches were screened, all before the feed went quiet at 10:32Z and the machine went down (93d923ffda3d). The day before, a full day of 336 touches, had shown only 4 intent touches (1.2 %), already near the floor.
why: The outage decided the miss. But even on a full day the floor of 3 was close: intent ran 4 on 10-08 and 1.2 % of touches, against the 4-10 % share the range assumed, so the lower bound was tighter than the week supported and a quiet full day could have broken it too.

what: The screen passed 0 of 4 coins on 2026-10-09 (0 %) against a range of 1-12 %. Only 4 touches reached the screen before the feed went quiet at 10:32Z and the machine went down (93d923ffda3d); 10-08 had passed 3 of 101 (3 %).
why: With 4 coins screened the metric could only take the values 0 %, 25 %, 50 % and so on, none of them inside 1-12 %, so once the sensor was down the forecast could not come true whatever the screen did. A pass-rate range needs a floor on the number screened, or voids below it; the measurement rule in 93d923ffda3d covers it.

what: 0 touches on 2026-10-10 against a range of 110-330. The sensor has logged nothing since 10:31:58Z on 10-09: the machine went down at 11:58Z, state/feeds.json (2508 B), state/positions.json (306 B) and monitor/heartbeat.json (82 B) came back all NUL bytes, and the guard has restarted the sensor every 5 minutes since 18:42Z 10-09 into the same JSONDecodeError at startup (guard.log through 06:05 Central 10-11, sensor-stderr.log). The 10-10 lesson said the run had backed the files up and reset them; it had not. The files still carry their 10-09 06:58 timestamps and NUL bytes, because every write route into the repo is denied in the unattended session, and today's attempt was denied the same way. Two full days (10-10, and 10-11 to 11Z) stand at 0.
why: The forecast, written 53 minutes before the machine went down, assumed the instrument runs; the model has no term for the sensor being dead, and a dead sensor scores as a market miss. The second miss in a row rests on a wrong report: the 10-10 run wrote that the files were reset when they were not, so nothing in the journal said the outage was still open. The range itself (full days ran 131-336) was fine. The repair is three one-liners the operator must run: write {} to state/feeds.json, [] to state/positions.json, {} to monitor/heartbeat.json; the guard restarts the sensor within 5 minutes.
rule: An unattended run that finds the sensor down says so in its reply and in the basis of every market forecast it writes, and a lesson never reports a repair the file bytes do not show: check the file after the command, not the command's exit.

what: RI-04 Amendment 3, the mark bug: the first twelve live closes (15:22Z-15:43Z) were booked on a mark that sold the position into the chain state as read, which does not contain the own buy of the book. A curve nobody else touched therefore marked -10.94 % (fees plus the entry impact paid twice) instead of -2.1 % (fees). Ten of the twelve closes were 60 s time exits, six of them at the identical -0.1641 SOL; the one stop (-27 %) fired early for the same reason and the one take (+30 %) was understated. No forecast resolved on them; all twelve are quarantined in journal/paper.RI-04-amend3.jsonl and never count.
why: The fill and the mark were written as two independent functions of the chain, and nothing asserted that a round trip on an untouched curve returns the buy less fees. The live book had no second instrument to disagree with it until the population replay (Amendment 2) ran the control fork over the same paths and came out 9 points higher per trade; the gap was the measurement error, not the market. Identical net on unrelated mints is the signature of an instrument artefact: a market produces a distribution, an instrument produces a constant. The belief B9 does not move, because the instrument lied and the market was not observed.
rule: Before the first counted trade of any contract, three invariants hold or the book does not start: (1) a paper round trip on a curve no one else touched books exactly the fee floor, pinned by a test (tests/test_population.py::test_time_exit_on_a_flat_curve_pays_fees_only); (2) the live book and the replay of the same contract over the same paths agree per trade, and any gap is a lesson owed before the count resumes; (3) a repeated identical net across unrelated positions is treated as an instrument fault first and a market fact second.

what: 6 of the first 40 RI-04 closes (10-23 15:59Z to 17:43Z, all under the Amendment 4 -5 % stop) netted above zero, a 15 % win rate against the 45 % bar: GOBLIN +0.715, THT +0.314 and MELANIA +1.442 by the take at +20 %, ADAM +0.230, CASINO +0.065 and CRIME +0.053 by the 60 s clock. The other 34: 18 stops and 16 losing time exits. 13 of the 19 time exits booked the identical -0.0318 SOL with peak 0 and trough -2.12 %, the fee floor of a curve nobody else touched inside the minute. 14 of the 18 stops never traded above entry, and their median hold was 8 s; those entered at 3.9-5.5K market cap (a dev buy already on the curve) against 2.9-3.3K for the flat ones. Cum net of the 40 was -2.34 SOL, mean -0.059, which trips G4; kill_ever reads 1. The market forecast it rests on (3ede51d728a5) stands at 34.4 matched launches a day against its 30 bar, so the market is holding and the miss is the book.
why: The 45 % carried Jack Duval's 41-61 % scalp win rates to a book that is the first outside buyer on a fresh curve. He bought coins that already had buyers; the book buys the create message. Two outcomes he never faced bound the win rate before any exit matters: a third of the entries draw no second buyer inside 60 s (a fee-floor loss that cannot be a win), and a quarter are curves the dev pre-bought and sold into within seconds of our fill. The win rate is capped by the share of launches that draw a second buyer, about half here, and the screen (a market-cap gate on the create message) selects nothing about whether anyone will buy next. B9 moves from 0.40 to 0.25: forty closes at mean -0.059 SOL with the structural first-buyer problem visible in 32 of 40 rows is more than one draw, though these ran under the -5 % stop and not the loop's own +20/-20 exits, so the belief as worded is not yet directly tested.
rule: Next contract: the screen must ask whether a second buyer exists, not what the curve is worth at creation: enter on the first outside buy after the create message (or after the dev buy), never on the create message itself, and log the share of matched launches that never draw a second buyer as its own market metric.

what: 18 of the first 40 RI-04 closes were stops (45 %), inside the bar of 50 % but a coin-flip forecast, so a bit owed. 19 left by the 60 s clock and 3 by the take. The stop was the Amendment 4 -5 % stop (7dd1424, 15:55Z 10-23), not the -20 % the basis assumed, and the first of the 40 closed at 15:59Z, four minutes later. 13 of the 19 time exits were untouched curves (identical -0.0318 SOL, peak 0, trough -2.12 %): with no trade at all, nothing could fire the stop. Of the 18 stops, 14 never traded above entry, median hold 8 s.
why: The basis pictured losers leaving by the clock a hair above -20 %. At -5 % every first sell fires the stop, so among curves that trade at all the stop share was 18 of 27 (67 %), well above half; what held the whole-book figure to 45 % was the third of entries that never trade inside the minute. The 50 % was a coin on a question the basis had no number for; the number it needed was the share of launches with no second buyer, and that number, not the stop level, sets the stop share under a tight stop.

what: Mean loss over the 34 losing closes of the first 40 was 0.152 SOL against the 0.12 bar (1.7 bits). The 16 losing time exits averaged 0.035 (13 at the fee floor of 0.0318). The 18 stops averaged 0.256, and only 5 booked under 0.12 (GOBLIN, FLAG, TI, BIDEN, Dax, troughs -5.6 to -7.3 %); 13 of 18 gapped past the stop. Six troughed beyond -20 % inside one 2-second mark (BILS -31 % and -27 %, TSTR -27 %, UKRAINE -44 %, GRAND -21 %, the coin named 1 at -43 %) and booked 0.32-0.65 SOL each, 2.89 of the 4.61 SOL all stops lost; their median hold was 8 s and they had entered at 4.0-5.5K market cap, a dev buy already on the curve.
why: The basis priced a -5 % stop as 0.075 SOL plus fees and treated a gap past it as a rare dev dump (p10 trough -14 %). On a fresh curve the first sell after our 1.5 SOL buy is the dev or a sniper unloading into a curve with almost nothing on it, so one sell moves the mark 20-45 % and the stop fills a third of the way down, not at -5 %. Thirteen of eighteen stops gapped: the gap is the typical stop, not the tail, and a stop level below the typical first adverse mark is cosmetic. The -5 % stop lowered the booked loss on the five curves that merely drifted, and did nothing on the thirteen that were sold into.
rule: Price a stop at the gap, not the level: the expected loss of a stop is the mean trough of the first sell after entry (about -15 % here, with a quarter beyond -20 %), measured from the population replay before the stop level is chosen, and no stop level under that mean is forecast as holding the loss near the fee floor.

what: The market-cap screen passed 159 of 488 matched launches on 2026-10-25 (32.6 %) against a range of 35-70 % (2.3 bits). The two days behind the range passed 354 of 662 (53 %) on 10-23 and 383 of 751 (51 %) on 10-24. What moved was not the market-cap gate: 'mayhem mode' rejections went from 28 (4 %) and 28 (4 %) on 10-23 and 10-24 to 121 (25 %) on 10-25, while mints without the 'pump' suffix held near 40 % (244, 283, 201). The next day, 10-26, passed 228 of 671 (34 %) for the other reason: non-pump mints rose to 320 (48 %) and mayhem fell back to 60 (9 %). 10-27 to 11Z reads 21 of 104 (20 %). The rate has sat near a third for three days running.
why: The basis treated the pass rate as one stable property of the market, near 52 % with a quiet Saturday allowed for, and set the floor 16 points under the two-day mean. The pass rate is the complement of two shares that move on their own: launches from other launchpads (no 'pump' suffix) and pump.fun's mayhem-mode launches, and mayhem alone took a quarter of one day after taking 4 % of each of the two days before. The 10K market-cap gate the forecast was named for rejected 2 of 488. Two days could not show either share moving, and the range gave no room for a share the basis had not counted.
rule: A pass-rate range for the RI-04 screen is built from its two rejection shares counted day by day (non-pump mints, mayhem mode), not from the pass rate's own mean: a share that has run 4-25 % of a day in the last week sets the floor, and the market table should carry both shares beside the pass rate.

why: The 10-09 rule on 576f3a962c68 said a ret24 forecast resolves only after the last screened coin's 24 h window has closed and the resolver waits for the window instead of spending a retry budget against it. RI-04 inherited the resolver unchanged: MK_TRIES is still 12 ticks, an hour, counted whether or not the quoter answered, so a quote outage at the deadline voids an answerable forecast exactly as the retry budget did under RI-03. The belief about the market, a median between a flat untouched curve and a dumped one, held (-6.7 %, -4.6 %, -13.5 % on the three days that have resolved); the instrument answered the question for it a third time.
rule: A due ret24 forecast waits on closed shadows, not on ticks: the resolver counts a try only on a tick where the shadow quoter answered, and voids only when every shadow of the window has closed and the median is still undefined. The operator should check the box's DNS: the shadow quoter has failed on getaddrinfo on 943 ticks since 10-06 and on every tick from 23:55Z 10-26 to 09:45Z 10-27.

what: The contract (Amendment 2) says the live book and the control replay should agree and a gap is a measurement lesson owed. The population report of 2026-10-24 printed the gap: control as the live book would run it +66.4 SOL on 312, live book counted -21.5 SOL on 321. No lesson was written and the 10-27 rulings built RI-05 on the control. On 2026-10-28 the join of journal/paper.jsonl to journal/paths showed why: the counted book fills at the chain state read at decision (duval.Book.enter), while the population control, RI-05 (five.entry_marks) and the 10-27 ruling fill at the create message's reserves and state that the counted book does too. The marks agree (195 of 196 closes of 10-27 reproduce within 0.02 SOL along the paths); only the entry state differs. 588 of 1150 counted entries (51 %) did get the message state; the other 562 filled after an earlier buyer, and refilling those 562 at the message state turns -45.6 SOL live into +208.8 SOL, PF 9.3. The control's whole edge (+97 SOL on 650 in out/five.md, +201 SOL over all 1150) is the earlier buyer's pump booked as if the book had preceded it.
why: A replay convention was written down as a fact about the engine without reading the engine: the 10-27 ruling's looked item said duval.Book.enter fills at the message's reserves, and the docstring of five.entry_marks repeated it, when Amendment 1 had moved the live fill to the chain read at decision on 10-23. The instrument that would have caught it, the population's control-versus-live line, printed the gap four days earlier and was read as the open first-buyer unknown instead of as the measurement lesson the contract names it. Ruled in decisions/2026-10-28-ri04-fill-grader.
rule: Every replay fills where the counted book fills: at the curve state read on chain at decision. The message's reserves are a counterfactual and the report labels them so. When the population prints a gap between the control and the counted book, the gap is the morning's first item and the lesson is written that day, before any ruling builds on the control.

what: The first-buyer question is answered as far as paper can answer it. Of 1150 counted entries 10-23..10-28, the 588 that filled at the message state (nobody had bought when the chain was read, median 0.0 s after the create) made -7.34 SOL, 13 % win, PF 0.71 under +20 % / -5 % / 60 s; the 562 that filled after an earlier buyer made -45.61 SOL, PF 0.50. Being first does not make the loop positive; it only makes it lose less. The counted book is KILL since 16:56Z 10-23 (G1 at the 11th close, G2 at 20:11Z) and stands at -52.47 SOL on 1153 closes.
why: B9 said the loop has positive expectancy after honest curve fills. The honest fill is the one the engine gets, and at that fill the loop loses whether or not the book is the first outside buyer. The earlier belief move (0.40 to 0.25 on 10-24) already named the first-buyer structure; this is the direct test on 588 first-buyer entries. What remains possible is a loop that is positive at the message state on the launches an earlier buyer took, which is a race the book was not in and paper cannot score. 0.10 rather than lower because the +20 % takes are real (22 of 196 on 10-27, +0.47 to +0.84 SOL each) and a different exit or screen on the same entries is not yet ruled out; that is a new contract id, not RI-04.

what: The fee floor of a real pump.fun round trip is 3.52 % plus 0.001 SOL, not the engine's 2 % plus 0.002 SOL: measured per account on chain across five 0.01 SOL round trips on 2026-10-28 (ops/fill_probe.py, journal/probe.jsonl). The whole amount enters the curve; pump.fun takes 1.26 % a side across three recipients, PumpPortal 0.5 % a side, the tx 0.000505 SOL; the token account's rent is paid and refunded.
why: src/duval.py froze PUMP_FEE at 1 % and TX_FEE_SOL at 0.001 from documentation, never from a landed transaction; Amendment 4 set the stop at -5 % as the fee floor plus three points, and the real floor (-3.5 % through PumpPortal, -2.5 % with a self-built tx) leaves 1.5 points, not 3.
rule: Every fee constant in a contract is measured on a landed transaction before the first counted trade; a replay's fee model is a hypothesis until a chain diff confirms it.
